g.text: Two statistics, one trade-off, one loss

g.data-cue-label: CCS described by two statistics along probe direction sigma-d displacement sigma-m midpoint
g.title: CCS is described by two statistics along the probe direction sigma-d-squared displacement and sigma-m-squared midpoint
g.desc: Describe CCS with two statistics along the probe direction: sigma-d-squared (how far pair is pushed apart) and sigma-m-squared (how far their midpoint sits from origin).
g.text: TWO STATISTICS ALONG THE PROBE DIRECTION θ̂
σ_d² displacement — how far the statement & negation are pushed apart
σ_m² midpoint — how far their midpoint sits from the origin

g.data-cue-label: its saturating sigmoid forces a trade-off maximize displacement minimize midpoint
g.title: Its saturating sigmoid forces a trade-off between spreading pairs apart and keeping midpoints small
g.desc: Because the CCS sigmoid saturates at both ends, it is forced into a trade-off: maximize the displacement while minimizing the midpoint.
g.text: probe in two competing directions at once:
keep the midpoint near the origin

g.data-cue-label: Midpoint-Displacement makes trade-off explicit with one knob lambda reproduces CCS or maximizes accuracy
g.title: Midpoint-Displacement makes this explicit with one knob lambda reproducing CCS or maximizing accuracy
g.desc: The Midpoint-Displacement loss writes this trade-off explicitly with a single hyper-parameter lambda: one setting reproduces CCS, another maximizes accuracy.
g.text: One knob, λ, sets the balance of the two terms:
Source: §3 Optimization target & the Midpoint-Displacement loss
